primaryText: Bǎobao fǎnfǎnfùfùde kū de māma xǐng-le.
translation: Mother repeatedly woke up as a result of the baby crying.

readings.name: the whole resultative is modified: repeated wakings
V1 alone is modified: the baby cried repeatedly until Mother woke once

comment: The V1-only reading is hard to access while the whole-event reading is available; (45) blocks the latter and recovers it.

translation: Mother repeatedly woke up as a result of the baby crying.

readings.name: the whole resultative is modified: repeated wakings
V1 alone is modified: the baby cried repeatedly until Mother woke once

comment: The compound's V1 cannot be independently modified: the components of a V-V resultative are inaccessible to syntactic operations.

primaryText: Bǎobao zài jiā lǐ kū de línjū xǐng-le.
translation: The baby cried at home until the neighbours woke up (next door).
context: The baby cried at home until the neighbours woke up next door.
comment: V1 of a V-de resultative independently modified by a locative.

primaryText: Bǎobao zài jiā lǐ kū-xǐng-le línjū.
translation: The baby cried at home until the neighbours woke up (next door).
context: The baby cried at home until the neighbours woke up next door.
comment: The minimal pair with (45): V1 of a V-V resultative cannot be independently modified.

translation: Zhangsan shot Lisi dead.
context: Zhangsan shoots Lisi, who is fatally wounded but does not die at once: the shooting and the dying overlap only at the moment the bullet makes contact.
comment: The scenario the trieventive analysis fits and the monoeventive and bieventive analyses do not (108).

translation: The baby cried until/ and as a result Mother woke up.
comment: The external argument interpreted as the agent of an unergative V1.

translation: I cut the onion in pieces.
comment: The external argument interpreted as the agent of a transitive V1.

translation: The dense rain made the earth dark by falling.
comment: The external argument interpreted as the theme of an unaccusative V1; the thesis cites the example from Li 1980 via Williams 2005.

translation: These clothes made big sister tired by her washing them.
comment: The external argument interpreted as the theme of a transitive V1; the thesis cites the example from Ren 2001 via Williams 2005.

translation: A cruiser sank as a result of Russian troops striking [it].
comment: V1 names the striking, the initial event of the causal chain (136), in which the Russian forces take part (138).

translation: A cruiser sank as a result of Russian troops causing [water] to enter [it].
comment: A pure causer: V1 names the seawater rushing in, the second event of the causal chain (136), in which the Russian forces take no part (140).

translation: The coach caused John to walk and as a result John got tired.
comment: A pure causer: the coach is not a participant in the walking. The thesis cites the example from Liu 2019.

translation: Zhangsan cracked the egg open.
comment: V1 'crack' is inchoative and has no causative alternant, so the external argument could only be a pure causer.

translation: That cutting board caused my knife to become dull as a result of cutting.
comment: An inanimate pure causer that is not an argument of V1.

primaryText: Zhè bù diànyǐng kū-hóng-le wǒ de yǎnjīng.
translation: My eyes became red as a result of crying about this movie.
comment: The external argument is the subject matter of the crying, a participant in V1's event, not a pure causer: onions or tear gas in its place are out (154).

primaryText: Nèi ge xiàohuà xiào-téng-le Zhāngsān de dùzi.
translation: That joke caused Zhangsan to laugh and as a result his belly hurts. / Zhangsan's belly hurt as a result of laughing about this joke.
comment: The external argument is the subject matter of the laughing; the thesis cites the example from Gu 1992.

translation: I cut something and as a result the knife became dull.
comment: The theme of the obligatorily transitive V1 'cut' need not be realised: the internal argument is the knife, V2's argument.

translation: I became poor as a result of {me/someone} eating this meal.

readings.name: someone else ate the meal I paid for

comment: The internal argument need not be the agent of V1.

translation: The audience cried as a result of {the audience/someone} singing this song.
comment: The internal argument need not be the agent of V1; the performer reading is the more plausible.

translation: The clothes were washed clean.
comment: An unaccusative V-V resultative whose sole argument is the theme of V1; acceptable whoever washed the clothes. The thesis cites the example from C. Li 2007.

translation: My knife became dull as a result of cutting.
comment: The sole argument interpreted as the instrument of V1.

translation: Zhangsan cried himself tired.
comment: The sole argument interpreted as the agent of V1: a subject-oriented resultative without a reflexive. The thesis cites the example from C. Li 2007.

translation: The handkerchief became wet from crying.
comment: The sole argument thematically unrelated to V1. Printed without a judgment mark (Sybesma 1999:16); the prose adds that some of the thesis's consultants judge it slightly degraded, especially out of the blue.

translation: Mother cried herself awake.

readings.name: Mother wakes from someone else crying

comment: An unaccusative resultative whose sole argument must be the agent of V1, a restriction the thesis leaves open.

translation: Zhangsan rode a horse and as a result {the horse/%Zhangsan} became tired.
context: A hybrid resultative, commonly described as a subject-oriented transitive resultative.
comment: The second reading is marked % for speaker variation; on both readings Tay analyzes the postverbal phrase as an argument of V2, a Locatum on the second.

translation: Zhangsan broke the vase by hitting it.
context: A transitive V-V resultative whose result verb is an intransitive change-of-state verb.
comment: The witness for two of chapter 8's three typological parameters: X is a verb, and a transitive resultative takes an intransitive X, unlike Japanese (674)-(675).
